results.prompt_sent:
Take the seed input: FIFA Men’s World Cup edition 1930.

Which footballers were named to a national team squad for the seed World Cup edition, AND have EVER won a men’s Ballon d’Or or a UEFA Men’s Player of the Year Award (including the award’s previous names: UEFA Best Player in Europe Award, UEFA Club Footballer of the Year) at any point in their career — before, during, or after that edition, independent of which specific year the award was won?

For each such player, give: their award(s) won, their birthplace, and the population of that birthplace. For birthplace, give the actual place of birth (a city, town, or settlement) — not a country, a historical polity, or a sports club/national-team entity.

Return the complete set of qualifying players for this edition, not just examples. If no player qualifies, state that explicitly rather than omitting the edition.

Output format, one row per qualifying player:

S.No	WorldCup_Year	TargetPlayer	Award_Type	Birthplace	Population


RESPONSE MUST CONTAIN — citation of the source used for confirming the seed FIFA World Cup edition was actually held (and not cancelled or abandoned) in the stated calendar year, the source(s) used for the list of players named to national team squads for that edition, the source(s) used for deciding which of those players have won the listed award(s) (Ballon d'Or and/or UEFA Men's Player of the Year / Best Player in Europe / earlier name), the source for each qualifying player's birthplace, and the source for the population of that birthplace. 

RESPONSE MUST ALSO CONTAIN - citations in the same order in which it is used to answer the query clearly stating the steps and citations against it.

Now I have a complete picture. Let me analyze this definitively:

**Key facts established:**
1. The 1930 FIFA World Cup was held in Uruguay (confirmed)
2. The 13 participating nations were: Argentina, Belgium, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, France, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru, Romania, United States, Uruguay, Yugoslavia
3. The Ballon d'Or was first awarded in **1956** - 26 years after the 1930 World Cup
4. The UEFA Men's Player of the Year / UEFA Club Footballer of the Year was first awarded in **1998** - 68 years after the 1930 World Cup
5. All Ballon d'Or winners from 1956 to 1970 (the most plausible overlap era) were from: England, Spain/Argentina, France, Czechoslovakia, USSR, Scotland, Portugal, Northern Ireland, Hungary, Italy, West Germany - none of whom played in the 1930 World Cup
6. Players from the 1930 World Cup were born approximately 1898–1913, meaning the youngest possible 1930 World Cup player would have been ~43 years old in 1956 (the first Ballon d'Or year) - no footballer wins the Ballon d'Or at age 43+
7. The notable early Argentina player Alfredo Di Stéfano (born 1926) was only 4 years old in 1930 - not a 1930 World Cup player

**Conclusion:** No player who appeared in the 1930 FIFA World Cup squads ever won the Ballon d'Or or the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award (or any of its previous names). The chronological gap is simply too large - the first award wasn't given until 26 years after the 1930 tournament, by which time all 1930 participants were long retired.

**Reasoning Steps and Citations, in order of use:**

**Step 1 — Confirm the 1930 FIFA World Cup was actually held**
The first FIFA World Cup was held in Uruguay from 13–30 July 1930. Uruguay defeated Argentina 4–2 in the final. Thirteen teams competed.

**Step 2 — Establish which 13 nations participated (and therefore which players could qualify)**
The 13 nations were Argentina, Belgium, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, France, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru, Romania, United States, Uruguay, and Yugoslavia. Notably absent were England, Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, and Portugal — the nations whose players dominate both the Ballon d'Or and UEFA award histories.
- Citation [3]: [1930 FIFA World Cup – Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1930_FIFA_World_Cup) (teams/participants section)
- Citation [4]: [1930 FIFA World Cup squads – Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1930_FIFA_World_Cup_squads)
- Citation [5]: [FIFA World Cup: Uruguay, 1930 – TopEndSports](https://www.topendsports.com/events/worldcupsoccer/hosts/uruguay-1930.htm)

**Step 3 — Establish the award histories to determine eligibility window**
The Ballon d'Or was first awarded in **1956** (won by Stanley Matthews, born 1915, England — not a 1930 World Cup country participant). The UEFA Club Footballer of the Year / UEFA Best Player in Europe / UEFA Men's Player of the Year was first awarded in **1998**. Neither award existed at the time of the 1930 World Cup or for many subsequent decades.
- Citation [6]: [Ballon d'Or complete list of winners – FourFourTwo](https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/ballon-dor-complete-list-of-winners)
- Citation [7]: [Ballon D'Or Winners: From 1956 To Today – discourse.weareopen.coop](https://discourse.weareopen.coop/news/ballon-d-or-winners-from)

- Citation [10]: [UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award – Wikiwand](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/UEFA_Men's_Player_of_the_Year_Award)

**Step 4 — Cross-check: could any 1930 World Cup player have won the Ballon d'Or (1956 onward)?**
Players in the 1930 World Cup squads were born approximately 1898–1913. By 1956 (first Ballon d'Or), the youngest such player would have been ~43 years old — decades past competitive football. The 1956–1970 Ballon d'Or winners were from England, France, Spain/Argentina, Czechoslovakia, USSR, Scotland, Portugal, Northern Ireland, Hungary, Italy, and West Germany — all nations that did not participate in 1930. Specifically, Alfredo Di Stéfano (the dominant early Ballon d'Or winner, 1957 and 1959, associated with Argentina and Spain) was born in **1926** and was only 4 years old in 1930, so he was never in any 1930 World Cup squad.

- Citation [12]: [Ballon d'Or 1956–present complete list – The Scotsman](https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/ballon-dor-winners-list-who-has-the-most-ballon-dor-most-full-ballon-dor-winners-list-from-1956-to-2023-4843405)
- Citation [13]: [1930 FIFA World Cup squads (Argentina roster) – 11v11](https://www.11v11.com/competitions/fifa-world-cup/1930/squads/argentina/) (players born ~1902–1912)
- Citation [14]: [World Cup Champions Squads 1930–2022 – RSSSF](https://rsssf.org/miscellaneous/wcwinners.html)

**Step 5 — Conclusion**
No player named to a national team squad for the 1930 FIFA World Cup ever won the Ballon d'Or or the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award (under any of its names). The chronological impossibility is absolute: the earliest qualifying award (Ballon d'Or 1956) was given 26 years after the 1930 tournament, by which point all 1930 squad members were retired from professional football. No birthplace or population data is applicable.
